claims.scope: StakingManager withdrawal queue, cancellation, and L1 operation processing

preconditions.text: User stakes 1 ETH and receives 1 kHYPE.; User queues a withdrawal, adding L1 Undelegate Command #1 to the queue.; The withdrawal is cancelled before pending withdrawals are processed via processL1Withdrawals.

evidence: 1. User stakes 1 ETH, receiving 1 kHYPE.

safety.text: Cancelling a pending withdrawal must also remove or invalidate its corresponding queued L1 undelegate operation so it cannot later be executed.; Total HYPE withdrawn from validators for a stake must not exceed the amount originally staked.

evidence: When a user queues a withdrawal, the StakingManager queues an L1 operation to withdraw HYPE from validators. Critically, If this withdrawal is later cancelled BEFORE calling processL1Withdrawals, the withdrawal request is deleted on L2(StakingManager), but the corresponding L1 operation to undelegate to staker remains in the queue. This can lead to a desynchronization between L2 state and L1 states.

Notice that this function only updates L2 state by removing the withdrawal request and returning kHYPE tokens to the user. However, it does not have a mechanism to know whether the undelegate request is still queued.
Hence, When the operator later processes the L1 operations queue with processL1Operations, all operations including those from cancelled withdrawals will be executed.

A vulnerability exists in the StakingManager contract if withdrawals are cancelled when they are still pending processing on L1. This introduces the possibility that a user can trigger multiple L1 withdrawal operations for the same stake, potentially withdrawing more HYPE than was originally deposited and breaking protocol accounting.
